HW 3: Lines, bands, priors, and groups

Due: Thursday, Feb 11 at 2:30 pm on Canvas · Size: light · Covers: Regression part 2

Start from the homework template, use ## Q1 to ## Q3 headings, and turn in both the .qmd and the rendered .html. Each question is graded 0 / 1 / 2 (missing / attempted / solid); answers in words count.

Q1 and Q2 build on your model from HW 2: same data, same priors. Load the fit you saved with file = instead of refitting. Q3 needs a categorical predictor. If your own data don’t have one, use sat.act from {psych} with SATV by gender (1 = male, 2 = female in this dataset), and say so.

Q1. Confidence vs. prediction

Make one plot with:

  • the raw data,
  • 50 posterior regression lines (add_epred_draws(ndraws = 50)),
  • a 95% band for the expected value (the “confidence” band), and
  • a 95% band for new observations (the “prediction” band, add_predicted_draws()).

This is your first publication-ready figure: make it meet the checklist (labels in words with units, a clean theme, a caption that says which band is which, saved with ggsave() at 6.5 inches wide).

Then in two or three sentences: why is the prediction band so much wider? Which band would you use to answer “what’s the average score for people with X = 30?” and which for “what score will this person with X = 30 get?”

Q2. How much does the prior matter?

Refit your HW 2 model with a deliberately bad prior on the slope: strong and centered in the wrong place. For example, if your slope is positive, use something like normal(-10, 1) scaled to your variables. Then:

  1. Plot the slope’s posterior from HW 2 and from this new model on the same plot.
  2. Did the bad prior move the posterior much? Using your sample size and the prior’s width, explain why or why not. What would have to be true about a study for the prior to really matter?

Q3. Groups

Fit a model with your outcome predicted by a categorical variable using index coding (y ~ 0 + group), with one prior for all the group means.

  1. Write the model in likelihood notation.
  2. Get the posterior of the difference between two groups, either with {marginaleffects} (avg_predictions() with by = and a hypothesis) or from the draws with {tidybayes}. Report it with a 95% interval.
  3. Convert the difference into a standardized effect (divide the difference by σ, draw by draw) and report its posterior.
  4. What is the posterior probability that the difference is greater than 0? (Count the share of draws where it is, or use hypothesis() with > as in class and read Post.Prob.) In one sentence, how is that different from a p-value? We’ll come back to this “probability of direction” in week 6.
